note: The wilds: how the open world's land looks and what is in it (roadmap: the wilds; core/game/game_wilds.gd for the look, game_wilds_sites.gd for landmarks, checked by tools/check_data.gd). Everything here is a pure function of the dynasty's seed and a tile: no die of the dynasty's is drawn and the land itself (height, water, nodes) is not touched, so towns, dungeons and the roads keep their guarantees. GROUND: each surface biome has `tones` (a translucent patch over the ground) and `decor` (small things such as tufts, flowers, reeds, boulders), each row a probability for a tile (`clump` makes it come in patches of that many tiles, `near` "water" wants water beside, `min_h` and `max_h` bound the height), and `trees`, the look a tree node takes in the biome (a birch, a pine, a willow, a dead tree, a giant fungus: the node is still the same oak or yew to gather). WATER has its own rows by body. AREAS: each `wilds` place of world.json has a signature drawn within its `radius` (full to `area_fade` of it, thinning to nothing at the edge, only on the place's own biome): its own tables, a `ring` of standing stones, a `lattice` of hedged fields, and its landmarks. Decoration thins to `road_floor` along a road and to nothing at a town. LANDMARKS: the world is cut into cells of `cell` tiles and each may hold one place of interest (`placement`: by biome, and by area where an area has its own), plus the `fixed` ones of an area at an offset from its anchor. A landmark is drawn from its `layout` (glyph names across, one row of tiles each, '.' for nothing) round its `center`, is found when the heir comes within `see_range`, and can be used from within `use_reach` tiles: an outcome is drawn from its `outcomes` on dice keyed on the seed and the landmark, once until `renew_gens` generations pass.

The hermit talks of {dungeon}, and the things that come out of it. {heir} listens, and learns something.
"Come in, sit," says the hermit. {heir} sits, and gets up rested.
The hermit says nothing for an hour, then gives {heir} {gold} gold for the company.
The hermit's door is shut, and a fine mist hangs round their hut; but a gift has been left on the step: {item}.
"The fen gives and the fen takes," says the hermit, and hands over a pouch of swamp-lights in a jar.
The keeper of the lantern points out to the grey water: "Wrecks, all along there. Take care what you take."
